issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking to establish tenancy or subtenancy status that depends on rent-control protections must be heard by the specially designated court, even when the landlord denies that the claimed relationship exists.
material_facts: A tenant had sublet premises to two other occupants, and the landlord obtained an eviction decree after the subletting was found unlawful.

The tenant and the two occupants later sued in a general civil court for declarations that the tenant was protected from eviction and that the occupants were lawful subtenants entitled to remain in possession.
The claims to continued possession depended on protections and status conferred by the rent-control legislation, rather than on rights that could be established independently of it.
The general civil court was not among the courts designated to decide claims arising under the rent-control legislation.
issues.conclusion: The general civil court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit. The special jurisdiction provision covered claims to tenancy status under the legislation even though the landlord disputed that status; the provision allowing a separate title suit applied to title arising independently of the legislation, not to a statutory tenancy claim.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 28 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, the courts specified in that section have exclusive jurisdiction over covered landlord-and-tenant suits and claims or questions arising out of the Act, including a disputed claim that the parties have a landlord-and-tenant relationship under the Act. Section 29A permits a separate suit in a competent court to establish title to premises where the title question does not arise out of the Act; it does not transfer jurisdiction over a status that exists only by virtue of the Act. Section 14 is relevant to the claimed statutory status of a lawful subtenant after the principal tenancy ends. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.rent_control_status_suit: A tenant or alleged subtenant brings a suit seeking recognition of status or possession under rent-control protections.
predicates.claim_depends_on_rent_protection: The claimed right to tenancy status or continued possession depends on protections created by rent-control law and cannot be established independently of those protections.
predicates.ordinary_court_not_designated_forum: The suit is brought in a court outside the class assigned to decide those rent-control claims.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks tenancy status or possession under rent-control protections, and it is brought outside the courts assigned to decide such claims, the ordinary court lacks jurisdiction.
